claim: Reuters documents shift toward robot intelligence and field-data acquisition
verifiedFacts: Reuters published interviews November 1 UTC with robotics founders and analysts describing a shift toward embodied AI software and training data.
Reuters cites ITjuzi's 93.5 billion yuan across 322 Chinese embodied-AI deals in the first half of 2026; this is a reported dataset, not independently audited here.
The report documents company-described robot work in battery testing and pharmacy order handling, with human checks in the latter.
inference: Traceable physical-action evidence and failure-mode receipts matter more than impressive robot motion demonstrations.
Client problem: buyers cannot compare robotic task success rates across conditions and unfamiliar environments.
Thesis movement: reinforces governed evidence and expands applicability to physical AI.
Advisory classification: CORE Seed Loom; INCUBATE Omni-Loom physical action proof; no robot build.
significance: Real task evidence and provenance become a differentiator as hardware makers pursue adaptable intelligence.
assumptions: Company-reported field successes represent actual repeatable deployments.
knownLimitations: Reported financing and success rates not independently audited; many examples remain pilots.
